title: Context engineering for coding agents in one minute
description: Most people think context engineering is some complex art. It really isn't. Your coding agent is just an LLM with a context window, and a harness like Claude Code overlays a system prompt and tool definitions you can't touch. The whole game is that anything that doesn't reach the context window literally does not exist to your agent. So your CLAUDE.md or agents.md file is the trunk, it loads automatically every single time, and from there you point to skills, scripts, MCP tools, and workflows like branches on a tree. Your agent follows the breadcrumbs out to the leaves and only loads what the task actually needs. That's progressive disclosure, and it's how you give an agent access to a hundred tools without drowning it in context up front. Get this one mental model and everything else about agent context clicks.
